text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana assured the three Baltic states yesterday that their NATO candidacy has not been ruled out.
- An unknown person attempted to kill a high-ranking customs official yesterday; the official received two bullet wounds.
SONUMILEHT
- Rural parties sent a letter to Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi, criticising some aspects of the coalition's policies but hoping for good cooperation.
- The Centre Party faction criticised corruption and the new anti-corruption law at a news conference; the law was described as inadequate and ineffective.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- More than 46,000 road signs need to be replaced at a cost of 138 million kroons.
- Scottish football fans were furious at the cancelled game on Wednesday after the Estonian failed to show up for a rearranged kick-off time.
- A German diving firm has been invited to enter the wreck of the Estonia ferry to search for the body of the Estonian captain.
POSTIMEES
- The Estonian chairman of the Estonia investigating panel does not support the proposed German diving expedition.
- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs is visiting Estonia.
- The government amended a regulation which would have mae 7,000 former Russian military illegal residents.
ARIPAEV
- Three insurance firms, Aeromet, Farret and Kalju, are to merged by their owner into one large firm to meet official requirements on share capital.
- The TV1 private TV company hopes to begin broadcasting on October, a start delated since the end of last year.
- The design for a new business centre was approved by Tallinn city council. It will be in the centre of the city and also house the headquarters of Savings Bank.
-- Riga Newsroom, +371 721 5240
